summary: Meridian is an Earth-observation and AI decision-support workspace that helps growers maximize farm revenue sustainably by balancing cover-crop soil protection against soil water availability for the following cash crop. While cover crops build long-term soil health, they consume moisture that can reduce subsequent cash-crop yields if terminated too late or planted in water-stressed soils. Meridian unifies live NASA satellite imagery (GIBS SMAP, VIIRS NDVI, GPM IMERG), NASA POWER 30-day precipitation and root-zone wetness, USDA NRCS SSURGO soil horizon profiles, USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer classifications, and U.S. Drought Monitor snapshots inside a 4-level zoom-adaptive H3 hexagonal map. Growers can draw custom field polygons, schedule cover-crop termination windows, and calculate unit-aware net returns and break-even yield thresholds. Finally, a predictive machine learning pipeline forecasts soil moisture and crop trade-offs while Meridian—an autonomous Mastra AI advisor—cross-checks user assumptions against regional USDA benchmarks to recommend profitable, water-smart rotations.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Meridian is a full-stack agricultural intelligence workspace that connects orbital Earth observations, soil survey data, predictive machine learning, and an autonomous AI advisor into a single workflow:

1. Four-Level H3 Geospatial Explorer (/): Partitions the contiguous United States into zoom-adaptive Uber H3 hexagonal cells (Resolutions 2 through 5). Clicking any hexagon queries live NASA POWER daily meteorology (MERRA-2 / GEOS-IT 30-day contiguous precipitation and 0–100 cm root-zone relative wetness) alongside USDA NRCS SSURGO soil profiles (0–100 cm available water storage capacity, sand/silt/clay fractions, organic matter, bulk density, pH, and saturated hydraulic conductivity). Users can toggle NASA GIBS layers (SMAP surface soil moisture, VIIRS NDVI vegetation index, GPM IMERG precipitation), U.S. Drought Monitor severity snapshots, and Regional Atlas county yield-effect research (486 Corn Belt counties).

2. Custom Polygon Field Planner & Economics (/planner, /economics): Growers draw exact field polygons using Terra Draw (with automatic geodesic area and centroid calculation) or drop sample points, request USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer (CDL) crop history, configure cover-crop species (cereal rye, winter pea, forage radish, multi-species mix) and termination lead times (0–60 days), and model net profit per hectare/acre alongside break-even yield changes.

3. Predictive ML & Mastra AI Advisor (/intel): A Python ML pipeline models future soil moisture dynamics and cash-crop versus cover-crop trade-offs from historical observations and NASA meteorology. Meridian—our Mastra AI agent—uses dedicated tools to inspect field telemetry, compare cash-crop economics, and validate user inputs against USDA ERS regional benchmarks so recommendations optimize sustainable revenue rather than relying on blind assumptions.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

Agricultural data is fragmented across government portals, scientific papers, and manual spreadsheets, leading growers either to avoid cover crops altogether (currently only 4.7% of U.S. cropland) or to manage termination blindly and lose cash-crop yield to water depletion. Meridian replaces disconnected tools with one transparent workspace that attaches exact observation dates, coordinates, spatial scales, and units to every figure—enabling farmers, conservation planners, and extension advisors to adopt cover crops profitably without compromising soil moisture.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

- Frontend & Geospatial Engine: Next.js, TypeScript, React, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui, deck.gl, MapLibre / OpenFreeMap, Uber H3, Terra Draw, Playwright.

- Backend & Data Pipeline: Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Pydantic, pandas, scikit-learn, MLflow.

- AI Agent & Orchestration: Mastra AI framework (apps/web/lib/meridian) with custom agronomic and telemetry tools, Turborepo, pnpm.

CREATIVITY & DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS

- Epistemic Transparency & Guardrails: Regional hexagons are explicitly distinguished from field boundaries, mapped soil capacity is separated from current moisture, and missing data is never zero-filled. In live use, Meridian automatically flags unrealistic yield entries against USDA ERS regional references before generating revenue advice.

- Privacy-First Offline Persistence: Growers require zero login; fields, plans, and economic models persist locally in browser storage with versioned JSON export/import and rollback protection.
